newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Fighting in Sri Lanka kills 33.
newsitem.headline: Fighting in Sri Lanka kills 33.

text.p: Fierce fighting between government troops and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels killed at least 33 combatants in north and east Sri Lanka, the Defence Ministry said on Friday.
The worst battle was at northern Puliyankulam, where 20 rebels and five soldiers were killed when the guerrillas attacked the troops with mortars on Thursday, the ministry said in a statement.

Government troops have been consolidating their positions south of Puliyankulam since two divisions, part of an offensive launched in May to open a strategic highway in Sri Lanka's north, linked up on Wednesday.
Twenty-eight soldiers were wounded during the confrontation on Thursday, the ministry said.

The statement said military intercepts of rebel radio transmissions indicated that five rebels were killed in a clash with troops in northwestern Mannar town on Wednesday. Two soldiers were killed in the clash.
In a separate incident on Thursday, also in Mannar district, three soldiers were killed by rebels at Semmantivu village, the statement added.

The LTTE are fighting a 14-year-old war for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE put the toll higher.
